A storm-tower library of open wrought-iron balconies spiraling up a narrow spire, shelves exposed to cold air and cloud-wrack, the city visible as a smear of light far below.
A library in an inverted tower dropping beneath a lake, its shelves lining the inner walls of a narrowing cone plunging downward, water pressing green against glass far above.
A palatial Baroque library of gilded galleries stacked six tiers high beneath a frescoed oval ceiling, marble busts watching from every level, the patterned floor impossibly distant below.
A nomadic tent-library of impossible interior scale, silk-hung shelves rising to a peaked darkness overhead, rugs covering a floor that seems to descend further with every step inward.
A bone-white ossuary-library carved from salt, shelf upon shelf of tablets and scrolls rising into a dome whose apex drips mineral water into a dark pool far below.
A cloud-library suspended in open sky, shelved platforms linked by rope bridges swaying at every height, the nearest solid ground invisible through mist an unknown distance below.
A ruined amphitheater converted to a library, concentric rings of shelves stepping down to a reading-pit at its center, crumbling archways framing open sky high above the uppermost tier.
A volcanic-cavern library of basalt shelves rising from a cooled lava floor toward a ceiling venting distant pale light, heat-scarred tomes packed into every niche of the towering walls.
